text:
Maya Patel: Heads-up — Acme Payments opened a ticket saying replies are suddenly terse after our recent model upgrade. They pasted before/after snippets showing examples removed.

Samir Khan: Can you drop the request they used? Need model id + params to reproduce.

Maya Patel: They called our hosted API with model `redwood-1.4` (rolled 2026-03-12T02:14Z). Their request (redacted) was:

```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <key>
{
  "model": "redwood-1.4",
  "input": "How do I validate a webhook signature?",
  "temperature": 0.0
}
```

Maya Patel: Before (on redwood-1.3) they got ~70 tokens including short Node/Python examples and a note about clock skew. After the upgrade they got a one-sentence answer (~20 tokens): "Compute HMAC with the shared secret and reject mismatches."

Samir Khan: Interesting. Temperature 0.0 usually forces deterministic output and can be concise, but if 1.3 returned examples at 0.0 and 1.4 doesn't, that's a behavioral change.

ops-bot: Deploy log: redwood-1.4 deployed canary->global 2026-03-12T02:14:22Z. Rollout ID r-20260312-14.

Jenna Ortiz: Two immediate possibilities: (a) model tuning reduced optional elaboration at low-temp, or (b) runtime post-processing (e.g., a brevity filter) accidentally toggled for some routes. Anyone repro locally?

Maya Patel: Reproduced with our account key: same terse reply when temp=0.0. When I set temperature=0.5 I get a longer reply with code snippets. Example runs attached in the support ticket.

Samir Khan: That suggests the model's deterministic mode favors terse tokens now. Could be a training or decoding change. We should quantify impact (how many customers use temp=0.0 and expect examples).

Jenna Ortiz: Action items:
- Support: collect 3-5 representative customer prompts that lost examples and paste raw requests and responses (Maya)
- Docs/Devex: add an entry to the changelog noting potential changes to deterministic outputs and recommend mitigations (bump temp to 0.2-0.4 or explicitly request examples in the prompt) (Jenna)
- Eng-ML: run batch eval comparing 1.3 vs 1.4 at temps {0.0,0.2,0.5} on how-to/howto prompts; measure presence of examples and average completion length (@eng-ml) (Samir)

Maya Patel: I filed SUP-11288 and pasted the before/after. Customer accepted a mitigation trial: they will try temperature=0.3 and report back.

Samir Khan: I'll create ENG-ML ticket and tag serving/runtime folks: ENG-ML-4321 "Investigate reduced elaboration at deterministic decoding for redwood-1.4". If model tuning intentionally changed behavior we should consider a labeled variant for deterministic customers or a rollback if customer impact is broad.

Maya Patel: Quick mitigation we can offer customers: (1) bump temp to 0.3; (2) include an explicit system instruction like: `system: When asked for instructions include a short example in Node and Python.`; or (3) set `max_tokens` higher so the model can emit examples even in deterministic mode.

Jenna Ortiz: Also check runtime defaults: are we applying any server-side overrides for temperature or a brevity flag per-customer tier? Samir, can infra confirm at-serving no post-process brevity flag was turned on during the rollout?

Samir Khan: Pinging @eng-infra to audit serving flags and any feature flags toggled during rollout.

ops-bot: Ticket ENG-ML-4321 created by Samir Khan: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-ML-4321

Maya Patel: I'll update SUP-11288 with our repro steps and the mitigation suggestions. Will follow up with the customer in 24 hours.

Jenna Ortiz: Good. If customer still sees missing examples after temp bump, we'll escalate to P1 and prepare a short rollback window. :warning:

Samir Khan: Noted. Also let's collect metrics for the percentage of requests with temp<=0.0 over the last 7 days so we can size the population affected.

Maya Patel: On it. Closing loop once I hear back from Acme.
